newsitem.title: UK: Barclays up in strong bank sector.
newsitem.headline: Barclays up in strong bank sector.

text.p: Shares in Barclays Plc led the UK bank sector higher on Tuesday, as some investors switched out of National Westminster Bank Plc and Barclays was squeezed higher amid a shortage of stock in the market, traders said.

Analysts said banks were in the front line of expected beneficiaries from low interest rates and were among the biggest gainers from reduced fears of a U.S. rate rise that boosted Wall Street on Monday.
"People just don't want to be out of the sector," said one market-maker. Barclays was up 13p at 924 by 1104 GMT while NatWest was down 4p at 664-1/2.
Other banks were higher with Lloyds TSB Group Plc up 4-1/2p at 376, HSBC Holdings Plc up 7p at 11.23-1/2 and Royal Bank of Scotland Plc up 6-1/2p at 495-1/2.
"The prospect of higher U.S. interest rates might have been a little worrying for UK bank stocks," said an analyst at one fund management group.
"But if any rise is just a one-off, and if Wall Street holds steady, there is no reason for bank stocks to worry."

He said Barclays and other banks were trading at a discount to the market in terms of price-earnings ratio, though NatWest was likely to remain more lowly rated because its expansion in investment banking risked increasing earnings volatility. And he said the bank sector could continue to advance if fears that they would repeat past lending mistakes proved mistaken.
"The sector has strong dividend growth," he said, "and if the banks are being more prudent on lending you have got to reckon they will improve their relative rating."
Yet not everyone was so positive.

David Poutney, analyst at Panmure Gordon, said he was a seller of Barclays. "It was the second best performing bank stock in the second quarter and there has got to be scope for profit-taking," he said.
